elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Revised 7.2 now reads "Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any commercial offer it receives," eliminating the disclose-and-match mechanic; Section 12.3 remains and independently confirms Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." No other operative provision imposes a best-terms obligation on Customer.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer MFN at all, so there is no scope to limit. The preferred outcome (no MFN) subsumes the fallback scoping requirement.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Customer MFN obligation survives in 7.2 or elsewhere, so no duration limit is needed.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the disclose-and-match obligation deleted there is no comparison mechanic requiring carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor-granted MFN pricing in Customer's favour is retained (redline guidance: keep any Vendor-granted MFN).
elements.evidence: The edit touches only the Customer-side obligation in 7.2; no Vendor-granted best-pricing commitment appears in the cited text and none was deleted.

reasons: The single operative change rewrites Section 7.2 to negate the Customer-side disclose-and-match obligation, which is precisely the MFN mechanic the rule targets; the preferred element is met in operative language rather than only in the comment.

Correctly treated as MFN rather than exclusivity: the original clause was a disclose-and-match mechanic and, post-edit, Customer remains free to engage other providers (reinforced by retained Section 12.3), so no double-flagging under an exclusivity rule.

Minimal: only Section 7.2 was altered; Section 12.3 and all surrounding allocation, timing, and commercial mechanics are untouched, and no survival tails, procedures, or extra requirements were added. Replacing the obligation with an express negation (rather than pure deletion) is a concise, same-length statement that avoids leaving a dangling section number.

Preserves intent: the edit removes an internal inconsistency with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created, and no Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour was disturbed.
Deterministic gates (operation applies, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with substantive review of the rendered text.
